findings.evidence: `rg`/`nl` shows the overclaims at lines 325-328, 472, and 509-514, while the signatures at lines 329-334, 473-476, and 515-529 assume only `(hU : IsPathHomotopyTrivial U)` or `(hU₀ : IsPathHomotopyTrivial U₀)`.
findings.fix: Rewrite those docstrings to say `path-homotopy-trivial set` and avoid promising neighborhood/SLSC hypotheses not present in the statements.
findings.issue: The docstrings for `Path.segment_rung_homotopy`, `Path.nullhomotopic_of_range_subset_pathHomotopyTrivial`, and `Path.paste_segment_homotopies_pathHomotopyTrivial_source` describe `U`/`U₀` as an SLSC neighborhood, but the declarations only assume an arbitrary `IsPathHomotopyTrivial` set, with no openness or neighborhood condition.

findings.evidence: Lines 297-300 claim each rung lies in adjacent `U`s, but the conclusion at lines 304-306 is `(∀ j, range (α j) ⊆ T.V j)` plus `(∀ i, range (α i.castSucc) ⊆ T.U i ∧ range (α i.succ) ⊆ T.U i)`.
findings.fix: State the exact result: every rung lies in its vertex neighborhood `V j`; for each segment, its left and right rungs lie in that segment's `U i`, so only interior rungs lie in both adjacent segment neighborhoods.
findings.issue: The docstring for `Path.exists_rung_paths` says each rung `αᵢ` lies in both adjacent segment neighborhoods `Uᵢ₋₁` and `Uᵢ`, which overclaims for the endpoint rungs; the statement only gives each rung lies in `V j`, and for each segment `i`, the two boundary rungs lie in `U i`.

summary: Several new docstrings still overstate the hypotheses of exported path-homotopy lemmas. Replace the neighborhood/SLSC language with the actual `IsPathHomotopyTrivial` set hypotheses and clarify the endpoint rung conditions.
